correctness.rationale: Necessity is by intracluster automorphisms and cross-component pointed bisimulations. Sufficiency explicitly defines root via a depth-two conjunction of diamond-of-support tests, then every singleton. All quantifiers include m>=2 and arbitrary positive root/terminal sizes; m=1 is proven separately. Falling factorial counts follow from independent labelled injections. Sharpness is witnessed by the (1;2,1) bouquet and exact depth-one equivalence. Actual finite checker verified 116 cases, 281347 colourings, with direct algebra closure in 5641 instances; finite experiments are not used as infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general K4 local-finiteness classification is about all finitely generated subalgebras being finite, automatically true for these finite frames, and does not bound their exact generator number. The height-two free algebra counts formula equivalence across every finite height-two partial order, not a fixed bouquet with complete terminal equivalence components.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The m=1 threshold and its count follow from the S4.3 theorem and are not claimed original. The m>=2 sufficiency needs an explicit depth-two formula rho that reaches two distinct terminal supports while being false at every terminal point; neither the linear-chain implication nor the disconnected S5 implication supplies this root separator. The published modal root-theory theorem shows depth-two distinguishability in a fixed equal-size one-root family but does not establish the all-singletons generating condition for heterogeneous root clusters or enumerate their labelled generating tuples. Its characterization gives relevant techniques and could imply special subcases, acknowledged as a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The structural criterion determines the minimum finite observational alphabet for full state recovery by Boolean modal formulas. The exact generating-tuple product applies to arbitrary terminal-size multiplicities. Adding a new terminal cluster can strictly decrease minimal generator rank (from 2 to 1), and every generating tuple admits depth-two reconstruction; this explains a genuinely branching phenomenon beyond linear-cluster generator criteria. For fixed terminal size s the rank is log_2(m)/s+O(1).
